uncertainty: Courier interest, language preferences, route relevance and repeat use have not been tested.
No comparison with participants' current alternatives has been performed.
Checker availability, translation accuracy and minutes per briefing are unknown.
No messaging, translation or hosting supplier costs are supplied. Stripe payment fees are supplier costs, not demand evidence, and payment processing is unnecessary for this free pilot.
The proposed €0 cash budget excludes unpriced human effort; no future payer or funding model is established.
dissent: A short free pilot can reasonably prioritize repeat interest over identifying a payer; requiring monetization now would be premature.
Manual checking is appropriate for discovery even if it limits autonomy, provided its time cost is measured.

uncertainty: No courier interviews, repeat-use observations or other market validation have occurred.
Preferred language, vehicle type, routes and existing information methods are unknown.
Source freshness, coverage, translation accuracy and correction latency are untested.
Delivery costs, checker availability and minutes required per briefing are unknown.
There is no payer hypothesis beyond a justified initial free-use experiment.
dissent: A free, tightly scoped briefing may merit testing before a payer is identified because repeat-use behavior can cheaply challenge the usefulness hypothesis.
Human checking may be an appropriate permanent safety control; full autonomy need not be the goal if measured operating effort remains acceptable.
